name: The Fillmore Charlotte
title: Fillmore Charlotte Wedding DJ & Host | Dan's Events
description: Planning a wedding at The Fillmore Charlotte? What the venue publishes and how I would plan hosting, DJ sound and warm lighting in a converted mill.
h1: Hosting, DJ and lighting at The Fillmore Charlotte
lede: The Fillmore Charlotte is a 100-year-old fiber mill turned music hall in Uptown, and its own site lists weddings among the events it hosts. It is a big room with its own house production, so the planning starts with who runs what.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: 820 Hamilton Street, Charlotte, NC 28206 (Fourth Ward, Uptown)

facts.label: Building
facts.value: A 100-year-old fiber mill, described as Charlotte's largest music venue

facts.label: Capacity
facts.value: Up to 1,700 guests per the venue; third-party listings give other numbers

facts.label: Rooms
facts.value: The Fillmore (main room) and The Underground

facts.label: Events
facts.value: The private events page lists weddings and receptions

p: The Fillmore's private events page describes a 100-year-old fiber mill in Charlotte's Fourth Ward and says the venue accommodates up to 1,700 guests. It names two rooms, The Fillmore, the main room, and The Underground. A Charlotte meetings listing describes the main room as a tiered layout in a roughly 25,000 square foot building with full-service event production, state-of-the-art lighting and sound, and custom menus. Capacity figures differ between listings, so confirm the number for a seated dinner. The Underground is the second room, and the venue does not describe how it is used for weddings.

sections.h2: Sound and hosting in a concert room
p: A room built for live bands is loud-ready, but a wedding is a different night: toasts that need to be heard, a first dance that needs a quiet room, and a dance floor that fills. I would sit down with the venue's event team early to learn whether outside DJs are allowed, and which parts of the house sound system I can use. The venue's pages publish none of that.
Because the room is tiered, I would plan where the host stands for introductions so every level can see, and keep speech and music levels tuned to a much bigger room than most weddings use.

The Fillmore is described as having state-of-the-art lighting and sound, so my first question is what the house rig already does and who may operate it. If my warm white fixtures add something, I plan them on separate circuits from the house systems. Low fog needs its own dedicated 30 A circuit; a concert venue may already run fog, but I would not assume it is available for a wedding.
The venue publishes no sparkler or fog rule, so I ask for approval of cold sparks and fog in writing.

Contact the sales team through the private events page, which lists floorplans, a one-sheet and a virtual tour. Ask about load-in, minimum spend, bar and catering, and which vendors are required, since the page does not publish them. Parking in Uptown deserves a plan of its own.

faq.q: Does The Fillmore Charlotte really host weddings?
faq.a: Yes. Its private events page lists weddings and receptions, and the inquiry form has Wedding as an event type.

faq.q: Can an outside DJ play at The Fillmore?
faq.a: The venue does not publish a rule. I would ask the events team in writing and plan around the house sound and lights.

faq.q: Who do we contact about a wedding at The Fillmore?
faq.a: The private events page lists a sales team at 980-266-6454 and an inquiry form with Wedding as an event type. Ask them for the floorplans, the one-sheet and the production and vendor rules.

faq.q: How big is the room for a wedding?
faq.a: The venue says up to 1,700 guests, while third-party listings give a range of numbers. Confirm the seated and standing counts for your layout with the venue.
